body:
Addresses the **mechanical half** of #998. That issue stays open for its semantic half — see "Deliberately not fixed here" below.

> No `Closes`/`Fixes` keyword on purpose: GitHub's parser ignores a parenthetical qualifier, so `Closes #998 (the mechanical half)` would auto-close an issue that is only half fixed.

## The catch-22

The archive gate demanded an adversarial review, and the review's own output then failed the gate.

`FindUnresolvedTags` walked **every** file in `specs/<id>/`, including the two files the review machinery writes there. The adversarial-review skill instructs the reviewer to check the spec for `[AGENT-DRAFT]` / `[AGENT-SUGGESTION]` markers — so checking writes those literals into the reviewer's output.

Measured on `HARNESS-072-pr-stewardship`, whose authored artifacts are genuinely clean:

| File | Size | Hits |
|---|---|---|
| `review-transcript.jsonl` | 552 MB | **3593** |
| `review.md` | 8 KB | **1** |
| `proposal.md` / `tasks.md` / `verification.md` / `features.json` | — | **0** |

3594 refusals, not one a real draft marker.

**`review.md`'s single hit is the sharper half, and #998 does not record it.** The hit is line 33 — the row reading `| No [AGENT-DRAFT] tags | ✅ | ... → none |`. The reviewer *certifying the spec is clean* is precisely what made the scan call it dirty. The only exit was `--force-with-drafts`, which disables the real check too, so every spec this tool reviewed either refused to archive or archived unguarded.

## Fix

`FindUnresolvedTags` skips `review.md`, the transcript, and its `.stderr` sibling **by exact name**. Everything else in the folder still scans, so an artifact added later (`design.md`, `notes.md`) stays guarded with no code change — a deny-list errs toward refusing an archive; an allow-list would silently stop guarding a file someone adds. That direction matches `ScanUnresolvedTags`' existing rule: *"both choices err toward refusing an archive, never toward passing one."*

Against the real folder: **3594 hits → 0, in 1 ms** instead of reading 552 MB into memory.

## Two adjacent defects, both found while proving the first

**`.gitignore` stopped matching at exactly the wrong moment.** The rule was `specs/*/review-transcript.jsonl`, and `*` does not cross a `/` — so it stopped applying the instant `Archive()` renamed the spec into `specs/archive/<id>/`, which is when the file is at its largest. Archiving HARNESS-072 would have tried to commit **552 MB, over GitHub's 100 MB hard limit**: the push could not have succeeded at all. Widened to `specs/**/`, verified against a real archived path.

This is a gap, not a convention — HARNESS-071's archived transcript is tracked only because it landed on 2026-08-14, one day before the ignore rule existed (2026-08-15).

**The staleness refusal named files that had not changed.** It recited all three contract files regardless, so an operator could not tell a rewritten acceptance criterion from a ticked checkbox without reconstructing the diff by hand — #998's "at minimum" ask. It now names only what actually moved.

## Deliberately not fixed here

The **semantic** half of #998 — exempting a change that the review itself demanded — is left open on the issue. It needs the reviewer to declare which files its findings target, which is a contract change to `review.md` and deserves its own design. `#998` stays open for it after this merges.

Also left: `--force-without-review` still asserts something false when what was overridden is freshness rather than existence. Same issue.

## Evidence

```
$ go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...
ok      (all packages)

$ golangci-lint run ./internal/spec/...        # pinned 2.12.2, matches versions.conf
0 issues.

$ FindUnresolvedTags(specs/HARNESS-072-pr-stewardship)
  before: 3594 hits (552 MB read)
  after:  0 hits, 1ms

$ git check-ignore -v specs/archive/<id>/review-transcript.jsonl
.gitignore:82:specs/**/review-transcript.jsonl   → matched
```

Tests pin both directions: review machinery output must not block an archive, **and** a live marker in an arbitrary added file must still refuse (proving the exemption is exact-name, not shape-based). Two existing staleness tests were tightened to assert the file that actually moved, rather than the old blanket phrase.

The `.gitignore` fix gets its own guard rather than a one-off manual check (`tests/gitignore-review-transcripts.bats`), since the expiry-at-rename is invisible in review — both globs look correct. **Observed failing before it was made to pass:**

```
$ sed -i 's|specs/\*\*/|specs/*/|' .gitignore && bats tests/gitignore-review-transcripts.bats
ok 1 review transcripts are ignored in an ACTIVE spec folder
not ok 2 review transcripts are ignored in an ARCHIVED spec folder (#998)
not ok 3 review transcripts are ignored in an ABANDONED spec folder (#998)
ok 4 the ignore rule does not swallow authored spec artifacts
ok 5 the transcript filename this guard asserts is the one the CLI writes
```

It asserts the destination path, not only the origin; that an over-broad rule does not silently stop versioning authored spec artifacts; and that the filename it protects still matches `TranscriptFile` in the Go source, so the guard cannot drift into protecting a name nothing writes.

## SDD skip rationale

A bug fix whose cause is measured, not designed. The 102 production LOC the gate counts are ~40 lines of logic and ~60 of explanatory comment (this repo's house style); the change adds no public contract, no dependency, and no design space — `FindUnresolvedTags` gains a three-name skip predicate and the staleness reason gains the filenames it already had in hand.

Scaffolding a spec folder for it would require an adversarial review of the spec before *it* could archive — a full SDD cycle to authorise a 40-line fix to the very gate that runs adversarial reviews. The cause here was established by measurement (the table above) before a line was written, which is what a proposal would have been for.
